t: Poor-quality locks on a godown and the absence of a night watchman are examples of:
e: Physical hazard relates to the tangible features of the risk; moral hazard concerns the character and conduct of the proposer.

t: The arbitration clause in standard miscellaneous policies applies to disputes regarding:
o: Whether the insurer is liable at all
The quantum of the claim where liability has been admitted
e: Arbitration is confined to disputes on the amount payable; if the insurer denies liability altogether, the insured must approach a court or other forum.

t: The monetary limit on complaints that an Insurance Ombudsman can entertain is currently:
e: The Insurance Ombudsman Rules, as amended in 2021, raised the limit to ₹50 lakh and widened the scope to all disputes about policy terms and service.

t: If the insured fails to submit the monthly declaration under a burglary declaration policy, the value for that month is taken as:
e: Non-submission is treated as a declaration of the full sum insured, which protects the insurer from under-declaration and raises the final adjusted premium.

t: A full-value burglary policy for ₹40 lakh is rated at ₹2 per mille. The annual premium is:
Which of the following stocks would attract the highest burglary rate?
e: Small, high-value, easily disposable items like mobile phones are most attractive to thieves; bulky low-value goods are rated lowest or on first-loss basis.

t: Cash at the shop counter is snatched by a robber during business hours. Under a money policy the loss is:
o: Covered under Section II (money on premises)
Covered only under a burglary policy
e: Section II covers money on the premises during business hours against robbery, hold-up and theft, and outside business hours only while in a locked safe.

t: A money insurance policy is a:
e: The insurer pays the actual amount of money lost up to the limits; it is not a valued or benefit contract.

t: The rate for Section II (money in safe / on premises) of a money policy depends mainly on:
o: The type and quality of the safe and the security of the premises
e: Premises cover is rated on the sum insured with regard to the class of safe, strongroom, alarms and watchmen; carryings determine the Section I premium.

t: A firm estimates annual cash carryings of ₹1.2 crore and the money-in-transit rate is ₹0.50 per mille. The provisional premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Premium = (₹1,20,00,000 ÷ 1,000) × ₹0.50 = 12,000 × 0.50 = ₹6,000, chargeable provisionally and adjusted on actual carryings.

t: A bank wants fidelity cover for all 200 staff of a branch without listing their names. The suitable policy is a:
e: A blanket policy covers the entire staff unnamed under one sum insured, avoiding endorsements on every staff change.

t: A fidelity guarantee policy differs from a surety bond in that:
o: FG covers the life of the employee
FG premiums are paid by the employee
FG is a two-party contract between employer and insurer, whereas a bond is a three-party arrangement among surety, principal and obligee
e: In a bond the surety guarantees the principal's performance to the obligee; in FG the insurer directly indemnifies the employer.

t: Section C of the Bankers Indemnity policy covers loss arising from:
o: Forgery or fraudulent alteration of cheques, drafts and other instruments
e: Section C responds when the bank pays out on forged or fraudulently altered negotiable instruments; employee dishonesty is Section D.

t: Under the Bankers Indemnity policy, money and securities belonging to customers but held by the bank in trust or safe custody are:
o: Covered, as property for which the bank is responsible
e: The policy covers money and securities belonging to the bank or held in trust, on commission or for which the bank is legally responsible.

t: Basic underwriting information required for a Bankers Indemnity policy includes:
o: Number of branches and employees, cash turnover and the internal audit system
e: The proposal seeks details of branches, staff, cash handled, security and audit controls, from which the basic sum insured and premium are determined.

t: Which statement about the Bankers Indemnity policy is INCORRECT?
o: It is a package policy for banks
Section D operates on a discovery basis
It covers loss of profit due to non-performing loans
e: Credit risk and trading losses are not insured; the other statements correctly describe the policy.

t: The values a jeweller must declare in the proposal for a Jewellers Block policy typically include:
o: Value in safe, value on display during business hours, value in custody of employees and value in transit
e: Each section is rated on its own sum insured, so the proposal captures the maximum values exposed on premises, in custody and in transit.

t: A public liability policy has an Any One Year (AOY) limit of ₹1 crore with an AOA:AOY ratio of 1:4. The Any One Accident limit is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). With ratio 1:4, AOA = AOY ÷ 4 = ₹25 lakh. Permissible ratios are 1:1, 1:2, 1:3 and 1:4.

t: A salesman leaves a bag of ornaments in a locked but unattended car and it is stolen. Under Section II of the Jewellers Block policy the loss is:
o: Not covered, due to the unattended-vehicle exclusion
e: Property in custody must remain in the personal custody of the specified person; loss from an unattended vehicle is excluded.

t: Limits under Section III (transit) of a Jewellers Block policy are usually fixed:
o: Per sending / consignment and in the aggregate
e: The schedule specifies the maximum value per sending by registered post, air freight or angadia and the aggregate for the policy period.

t: Which of the following is NOT one of the four sections of the standard Jewellers Block policy?
o: Property in custody of specified persons
e: The four sections cover property on premises, in custody, in transit and trade furniture/fittings; consequential loss is not covered.

t: Claims for jewellery under Section III (all risks) of the Householder's policy are settled on the basis of:
o: Market value at the time of loss, subject to the sum insured
Agreed value declared by the insured
e: The section is on indemnity basis; valuation reports help fix the sum insured but the claim is the market value at the time of loss within the sum insured.

t: The family's bicycle is stolen from the compound of the house. The relevant section of the Householder's policy is:
o: Section V – Breakdown of domestic appliances
e: Section VII covers pedal cycles against theft, accident and fire, with third-party liability; Section II applies to contents inside the dwelling.

t: The fire section of a Shopkeeper's policy covers:
o: Building and contents (stock, furniture, fixtures) against fire and allied perils
e: The fire section mirrors the standard fire policy for the shop building and its contents; cash is covered under the money section.

t: The premium for seven sections of a Householder's policy totals ₹4,000 before discount. After the package discount, the premium payable is:
e: Six or more sections earn a 20% discount: ₹4,000 − ₹800 = ₹3,200. Four sections would earn 15%.

t: Optional covers available under the standard Bharat Griha Raksha policy include:
o: Cover for valuable contents (jewellery, etc.) on agreed value and personal accident for the insured and spouse
Motor insurance for the family car
e: Beyond building and general contents, the product offers two optional covers: valuable contents on agreed-value basis and PA for the insured and spouse.

t: Stock valued at ₹20 lakh is insured for ₹10 lakh under a full-value burglary policy. Burglars steal stock worth ₹4 lakh. The amount payable is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The policy is subject to average: payable = (10/20) × ₹4 lakh = ₹2 lakh, since the insured is 50% under-insured.

t: An organiser of an outdoor cricket match is worried that rain will wash out the event. The suitable cover is:
e: Event cancellation (including pluvius cover) indemnifies irrecoverable expenses or loss of revenue if the event is cancelled or abandoned due to adverse weather.

t: Pet dog insurance normally pays on:
o: Death of the dog due to accident or disease (mortality cover)
e: The core cover is mortality; vet fees and theft may be available as extensions, but prizes are not insured.

t: Which of the following is excluded under an all-risks (valuables) policy?
o: Loss due to wear and tear, moth, vermin or gradual deterioration
e: All-risks policies cover fortuitous loss or damage but exclude inevitable deterioration, wear and tear, and inherent vice.

t: Aviation third-party legal liability insurance covers:
o: Injury or damage to persons and property on the ground or in other aircraft caused by the insured aircraft
Injury to passengers of the insured aircraft
e: Third-party liability is distinct from passenger legal liability, crew PA and hull cover.

t: A sports insurance policy for a professional sportsperson may include:
o: Personal accident, loss of earnings due to injury, sports equipment and third-party liability
e: Sports insurance is a package addressing the sportsperson's main exposures: injury, loss of income, equipment and liability.

t: A Personal Accident policy is a:
o: Benefit policy paying agreed sums on specified contingencies
e: PA pays fixed amounts (CSI or percentages) irrespective of the actual financial loss, so it is a benefit policy, not indemnity.

t: A PA insured with CSI ₹4 lakh loses the sight of one eye in an accident. The benefit payable is:
e: Loss of sight of one eye is permanent partial disablement at 50% of CSI = ₹2 lakh.

t: A teacher fractures her leg, is confined to bed for six weeks and then returns to work. The PA benefit payable is:
e: TTD applies when the insured is temporarily and totally prevented from attending to her usual occupation, paid weekly for the period of disablement.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: A PA insured dies in the crash of a private chartered aircraft that he was piloting. The claim is:
o: Excluded, as flying other than as a fare-paying passenger on a licensed airline is not covered
e: PA policies exclude aviation risks except as a fare-paying passenger in a regularly scheduled aircraft; piloting is excluded.

t: The cumulative bonus under a PA policy does NOT apply to:
e: Cumulative bonus enhances the capital sum insured for death and permanent disablement only; TTD is based on the basic CSI.

t: The maximum period of cover under the Employment and Study plan of the Overseas Mediclaim policy is normally:
e: E&S policies can be issued for up to 12 months and extended up to a total of two years, unlike B&H which is limited to 180 days.

t: Dental treatment under an Overseas Mediclaim policy is:
o: Covered only for emergency treatment to relieve acute pain to natural teeth
e: Only emergency dental treatment for immediate relief of pain is covered, usually within a sub-limit; routine and cosmetic dental work is excluded.

t: The period of cover under an overseas travel policy commences:
o: When the insured leaves India and ends on return to India or expiry of the policy, whichever is earlier
e: Cover is linked to the journey: it attaches on departure from India and ceases on return or on the expiry date, whichever is earlier.

t: Sericulture (silkworm) insurance covers loss due to:
o: Death of silkworms / loss of cocoon crop due to disease, accident, fire, flood and similar perils
e: The policy indemnifies the rearer for loss of the cocoon crop by fortuitous causes; price and market risks are excluded.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: Failed well insurance indemnifies the farmer for:
o: Loss of crop due to drought
The cost of drilling a borewell that fails to yield water
e: The policy reimburses the expenditure on boring when the well turns out to be dry or yields insufficient water.

t: A cow is insured for ₹60,000 (market value at inception). It dies of disease after four months, when its market value is ₹50,000. The claim payable is:
e: Cattle insurance pays the market value at the time of death or the sum insured, whichever is less, so ₹50,000 is payable.

t: Under the rules framed under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, the insurer's liability is capped at:
o: ₹5 crore per accident and ₹15 crore per year
₹10 crore per year without per-accident limit
e: The policy limit must be not less than the owner's paid-up capital (maximum ₹50 crore), while the insurer's liability is limited to ₹5 crore per accident and ₹15 crore per year; the Environmental Relief Fund meets relief beyond that.

t: A surgeon's liability for injury caused to a patient by a negligently performed operation is insured under:
o: Professional indemnity policy for medical practitioners
e: PI covers legal liability for errors, omissions or negligence in rendering professional services; public liability covers accidents at premises.

t: A goods transport operator's liability to consignors for loss of goods entrusted to him is insured under a:
e: Carrier's legal liability covers the transporter's liability under the Carriage by Road Act and common law for goods in his custody.

t: The portion of each risk that an insurer keeps for its own account is called its:
e: Retention is the net amount kept; the cession is the part passed to the reinsurer, and a 'line' is a multiple of retention used in surplus treaties.

t: Reinsurance (ceding) commission under a proportional treaty is:
o: Paid by the cedant to the reinsurer
Paid by the reinsurer to the cedant to compensate for acquisition and administrative costs
e: Since the reinsurer shares the premium proportionately, it pays the cedant a commission to cover the costs of acquiring and managing the business.
